note: Each item was checked against a primary source where one exists. Confirmed = matches the primary source. Corrected = the site's value was wrong or incomplete; corrected_value holds the right one. Unverifiable = no primary source found; the verify flag stays on. General information only.

items.claim: China removed duties on Australian barley from 5 Aug 2023
items.value: MOFCOM Announcement No. 29 of 2023, dated 4 Aug 2023, effective 5 Aug 2023

items.claim: China removed duties on Australian wine from 29 Mar 2024
items.value: MOFCOM Announcement No. 11 of 2024, dated 28 Mar 2024, effective 29 Mar 2024

items.claim: Provisional wine deposits from late Nov 2020
items.corrected_value: Provisional measures applied from 28 Nov 2020; final duties from 28 Mar 2021 (stated in MOFCOM Ann. No. 11 of 2024 review ruling)

items.claim: CMPTI passed 11 Feb 2025, effective 1 Jul 2027
items.value: Passed both Houses 11 Feb 2025; Royal Assent 14 Feb 2025 (Act No. 9 of 2025); offset available for production 1 Jul 2027 to 30 Jun 2040

items.claim: CMPTI announced in the 14 May 2024 Budget
items.note: Confirmed via PM release and Budget Paper 1 search results; release page not opened directly.

items.claim: EPBC reforms Royal Assent 1 Dec 2025
items.value: Environment Protection Reform Act 2025 (No. 68, 2025) assented 1 Dec 2025. Senate passed with amendments 27 Nov 2025; finally passed both Houses 28 Nov 2025. Schedule 1 Parts 1-2 commence by Proclamation or automatically 12 months after assent; NEPA-linked parts 1 Jul 2026
items.note: CORRECTIONS.md says a tranche commences 20 Feb 2026; not checked against a Proclamation, keep flagged.

items.claim: WA DMIRS/DEMIRS -> DMPE from 1 Jul 2025
items.value: DMPE exists and regulates mining/petroleum; its first Annual Report 2025-26 marks its first year (wa.gov.au announcement 23 Nov 2026)
items.note: Exact 1 Jul 2025 start date not found stated on a page opened; consistent with a first year ending FY2025-26. Human check of the WA Government Gazette advised.

items.claim: Qld regulator renamed NRMMRRD effective 1 Jul 2025
items.corrected_value: Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development established 1 Nov 2024 (Public Service Departmental Arrangements Notice (No. 9) 2024), not 1 Jul 2025

items.claim: NT split: Mining & Energy plus Lands/Planning/Environment, effective 1 Jul 2025
items.corrected_value: NT Department of Mining and Energy was established in September 2024, not 1 Jul 2025. Lands/Planning/Environment department name for environmental licences not re-checked

items.claim: NSW Resources within DPIRD, effective 1 Jul 2025
items.corrected_value: NSW Resources is a division of the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (confirmed). Reported start is 1 Jul 2024, not 1 Jul 2025 (from NSW Government release via search; the release page did not render)

items.claim: BHP's Chinese name is 必和必拓
items.value: BHP China site is titled 必和必拓

items.claim: Arafura is now Arafura Rare Earths
items.value: Arafura Resources Limited changed its name to Arafura Rare Earths Limited (ASX: ARU) after the 20 Oct 2022 AGM, effective around 1 Nov 2022
items.note: Effective date from search summary of the company notice; open the PDF to confirm the exact date.

items.claim: China rare earth export control suspension extended to 10 Jan 2027
items.value: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2026 (9 Nov 2026): Announcements 55-58 and 61-62 of 2025 stay suspended from 11 Nov 2026 to 10 Jan 2027. April 2025 controls on seven rare earths (Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y) remain in force

items.claim: CMRG/BHP dispute resolved Apr 2026; same-day match 22 Apr 2026
items.value: BHP Operational Review for the quarter (ASX, 22 Apr 2026 8:30 am AEST): 'We have concluded iron ore sales contract negotiations with the China Mineral Resources Group (CMRG).'
items.note: The 14 Apr 2026 'easing' date in CORRECTIONS.md is not confirmed by a primary source; stays flagged.

items.claim: CMRG halt on BHP Jimblebar fines began week of 22 Sep 2025; Jingbao added later
items.corrected_value: Reported first on 19 Sep 2025 (Bloomberg) for Jimblebar Blend Fines; widened to Jingbao fines around 21 Nov 2025 (Bloomberg). Reporting only: CMRG directives are not published

items.claim: China Energy coal purchase ~6 Jan 2023
items.value: Reuters exclusive dated 6 Jan 2023: China Energy Investment Corp placed an order for Australian coal, after Beijing allowed four firms to resume imports (Reuters, 5 Jan 2023)
items.note: Press report based on sources; there is no company or customs primary record. Keep the flag.

items.claim: Coal restrictions: May 2020 verbal notice, Oct 2020 start, 3 Jan 2023 easing, 14 Mar 2023 full removal
items.corrected_value: Oct 2020 verbal notice to stop imports (S&P Global, 9 Oct 2020); easing for four state firms reported 5 Jan 2023 (Reuters), not 3 Jan; all companies allowed reported 14 Mar 2023 (Bloomberg). No May 2020 primary or press source found. China never announced the measure

items.claim: Critical Minerals Strategy 2023-2030 released 20 Jun 2023
items.value: Minister King media release 20 Jun 2023

items.claim: Second Northern Minerals FIRB disposal orders from 18 Jun 2026
items.value: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers (Disposal of Interests in Northern Minerals Limited) Orders (No. 1) 2026 (F2026N00326), signed 17 May, registered 18 May 2026, commencing 18 Jun 2026 (31st day after registration); six holders, 1,678,895,780 shares, to divest within 14 days of commencement
items.note: Registration confirmed on the Federal Register and NTU ASX release of 18 May 2026; the 18 Jun commencement is from McCullough Robertson's summary because the register text did not render. Check section 2 of the instrument.

items.claim: NVIDIA H20 licence requirement
items.value: NVIDIA Form 8-K: on 9 Apr 2025 the US Government said H20 exports to China (incl. HK, Macau) need a licence; on 14 Apr 2025 it said this would apply indefinitely; up to US$5.5bn Q1 FY26 charges. Filed 15 Apr 2025

items.claim: NVIDIA H20 shipment/production halts
items.value: Reported 22 Aug 2025 (The Information, Reuters): NVIDIA told suppliers (incl. Amkor, Samsung; Foxconn asked) to halt H20 work after Chinese authorities discouraged purchases. Press reporting, not a company filing

items.claim: Whitehaven is GICS Energy, not Materials
items.value: GICS Energy (Coal & Consumable Fuels); in the S&P/ASX 200 Energy index (XEJ)
items.note: S&P constituent lists need a login; classification confirmed from secondary lists. Recheck at each quarterly rebalance.

items.claim: ASX settles T+2 (not T+1)
items.value: ASX cash equities settle T+2. ASX plans to resume T+1 industry engagement in 2027; T+1 would follow CHESS Release 2 (indicative 2029)
